description: Outline a payment-gateway style workload aimed at PCI DSS scoping for card-not-present or API-driven payments. Azure Front Door with Web Application Firewall (WAF) sits at the edge to absorb bot traffic, apply OWASP-oriented rules, and terminate TLS before traffic reaches regional Azure Container Apps that host stateless payment orchestration. Azure Key Vault stores keys, certificates, and optional HSM-backed material so secrets never live in environment variables or container images—addressing common PCI DSS expectations around key management, access separation, and auditability. This template is for architecture analysis: it explains *why* these components reduce cardholder data environment (CDE) sprawl and support compensating controls around segmentation, not a self-attestation of PCI compliance.
constraints: Primary account data (PAN, sensitive authentication data) must not be persisted in application logs, APM traces, or Front Door raw logs; tokenization or PSP-hosted fields preferred where feasible.
Secrets, signing keys, and TLS certificates must be sourced from Azure Key Vault with least-privilege RBAC and no long-lived shared credentials in Container Apps configuration.
Front Door WAF must be enabled on routes that accept payment-adjacent traffic; default-deny and rate limits documented for assessor review.
requiredCapabilities: Azure Front Door with WAF for global edge protection and TLS termination
Azure Container Apps for horizontally scaled, revision-based compute behind private or controlled ingress
Azure Key Vault for secrets and keys with managed identity access from Container Apps
Integration with a PCI-validated payment service provider (PSP) or token vault when raw card data would otherwise enter the CDE
assumptions: Scope reduction (network segmentation, tokenization) is explicitly documented so QSA review can bound the CDE.
Observability pipelines redact or drop fields that could contain PAN before central storage.
topologyHints: Edge: Front Door -> origin (Container Apps ingress or internal load balancer); keep payment microservices out of shared multitenant clusters without documented isolation.
Separate environments so production keys and PSP credentials never serve non-prod traffic.
securityBaselineHints: Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendations on exposed management planes and container registries feed PCI vulnerability management evidence.
Break-glass access to Key Vault and production Container Apps revisions is ticketed and logged for PCI access reviews.
